description: Port town overworld — no building open, character visible

detection.notes: hamburger visible OR (no home, no back, port name readable in top-left)

description: Inside any building (market, harbour, bank, castle, etc.)

detection.notes: home button visible; screen title identifies sub-type

exits.note: open a building sub-menu (Recruit Crew, Purchase, Sell, Deposit, ...)

description: A building sub-menu screen (Recruit Crew, Purchase, Sell, Deposit, ...). One level deeper than the building's main pane.

detection.notes: back arrow visible top-left; screen title is a known sub-menu name (Purchase, Sell, Recruit Crew, Deposit, Withdraw, ...)

exits.note: back out one level to the building's main pane.  Only navigation exit — tap_home is intentionally NOT registered because skipping straight to overworld abandons in-progress transactions (e.g. tapping Home from the Recruit Crew sub-menu silently drops the recruit transaction).  recover_to_port_overworld therefore goes sub_menu -> press_back -> building -> tap_home (2 hops), preserving any context that was committed before the recovery fired.

detection.notes: home button visible; port map visual chrome; building icons visible

description: World map overlay showing all ports

detection.notes: home button visible; 'World Map' in top-left title OCR

description: Hamburger side panel — shows game sections (guild, auction, combat…)

detection.notes: hamburger ≡ replaced by × at same position (2280-2400, 5-80); building list shows menu items: guild/auction/combat/collection/lighthouse/assault/production/enhance/rank/friend (≥2 match)

description: Open sea — sailing HUD visible. Two sub-cases: sailing (destination set) or idle (no destination). Both navigable.

detection.notes: sailing HUD keywords visible: 'days of sailing', zone label, wind speed

description: Idle/cinematic sea view — HUD hidden. Tap to restore HUD.

detection.notes: no HUD, no port name, no home button

description: The game's idle standby lock — a FULL-SCREEN takeover after inactivity. Nothing of the previous world survives on screen, which is what makes it a state rather than a popup. Its exit action is named on the screen itself; its destination is not knowable from here.

detection.notes: 'Slide up to unlock' prompt over a dark radial emblem. The title reads 'On Standby at Sea' or a port name — DESCRIBING THE STANDBY MODE, NOT the fleet's position: live 2026-08-26 it read 'On Standby at Sea' with server 'Atlantic Ocean' while the fleet was tied up in Svear Village. Never route on that wording.

exits.note: Destination UNKNOWN — the swipe returns to whatever world the bot was in. Re-perceive to find out; a remembered previous state is a belief, and beliefs are what go stale. Same shape as `loading`.
